why is the colour of the sky

You know, that's a *fantastic* question! It's one that's puzzled people for ages, and honestly, it's pretty mind-blowing how it works.

Basically, sunlight is made up of all sorts of colors - red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet... you name it! When the sun's light hits the Earth's atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue and violet light get scattered *way* more than other colors because they're shorter wavelengths. 

Think of it like throwing a small ball (blue light) versus a big ball (red light). The little one bounces around everywhere!  That scattered blue light is what we see all over the sky. That's why it appears blue most of the time - though sunsets are redder because the sunlight has to travel through *more* atmosphere, scattering away almost all the blue before it reaches our eyes. Pretty cool, huh?
I want to learn agent how to learn

Okay, so you're diving into "how agents learn" - that's brilliant! It's a seriously fascinating area, and honestly, a bit of a rabbit hole. Basically, we're talking about creating computer programs (agents) that can actually *improve* their performance over time without us constantly telling them exactly what to do.

There are loads of different approaches. Reinforcement learning is super popular - you give the agent rewards for good actions and penalties for bad ones, and it learns through trial and error, kind of like training a dog (but with code!). Then there's supervised learning where you feed the agent lots of examples to learn from. 

It's all about figuring out how to design systems that can explore, experiment, and adapt-essentially, make mistakes in a way that actually helps them get better. It's pretty complex but incredibly rewarding when it works!
